public_rationale: On November 17, 2023, OpenAI's board announced that it had lost confidence in Altman's ability to lead the company [e1]. OpenAI's March 8, 2024 summary of the WilmerHale review reported that a breakdown in trust between the board and Altman precipitated the November 17 firing [e2]. These accounts support the factual assertion that leadership tensions preceded and continued into the firing [e1, e2].
limitations: The assessment covers the assertion about tensions. Marcus's dislike of the 'clownish board theory' is an opinion; this outcome does not establish board competence or justify the firing.
Whether Ilya Sutskever felt left out is expressly unnecessary to the assertion and is not established by these records.
The records do not establish when the tensions began or every issue involved.
Both sources are OpenAI disclosures. The published review summary does not supply the underlying documents or interview records.

whether or not Ilya felt out

our_interpretation: The checkable assertion is that tensions existed within OpenAI's leadership before Altman's firing. The plain reading includes strained relationships or persistent disagreements between management and the board.
The target period is a snapshot on November 17, 2023, immediately before and at the firing discussed in the post. The claim does not specify when the tensions began.
Marcus's dislike of the 'clownish board theory' is a stated opinion. This assessment does not establish the board's competence or whether firing Altman was justified.
'Whether or not' expressly makes Ilya's feelings unnecessary to the assertion; it is not a condition that must occur.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable contemporaneous records or retrospective accounts establish leadership disagreements or a strained board-management relationship continuing into Altman's November 17, 2023 firing.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records establish that leadership relations were cooperative immediately before the firing and that the alleged ongoing tensions did not exist.
